subject: Intermittent strange tokens in generation — can't reproduce on our side
messages:
From: Nadia Campos <nadia@orionhealth.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Strange '###' tokens appearing in generated notes

Hi Kimberly,

We've started seeing occasional outputs from the Redwood API where the generated clinical note contains repeated '###' sequences mid-sentence, e.g. 'The patient reports nausea ### and vomiting.' It's intermittent (~1-2% of calls) and only started last week. I attached a small snippet of the response and the prompt we used.

We rely on clean JSON/markdown output for our downstream parsing. This artifact is causing our pipeline to treat the generation as malformed. Can you confirm whether this is coming from the model, a tokenization issue, or something on our side? Sample request id included in the attached file.

Thanks,
Nadia Campos
Product Owner, Integrations
Orion Health

Attachment: response_snippet.txt (contains: prompt + response + request_id: 20270429-OR-88-7f3)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Campos <nadia@orionhealth.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-30T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Strange '###' tokens appearing in generated notes

Hi Nadia — thanks for the report and for attaching the snippet. We're looking into this now.

Quick asks that will speed up triage:
- Can you share a handful of additional request_ids (if you have them) and approximate timestamps (UTC)?
- Are these calls using a streaming client or non-streaming HTTP responses?
- Are you pinning a model version or using our catalog alias?

I've looped in Rishi (runtime) and Monica (support ops). We'll replicate the request and check platform logs for any malformed tokenization, caching edge cases, or partial stream delivery.

If this is high priority for you we can schedule a short debug session this afternoon.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Nadia Campos <nadia@orionhealth.io>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Strange '###' tokens appearing in generated notes

Quick triage notes (I ran a first-pass repro):

> Reproduction attempt: I replayed the prompt from response_snippet.txt against the exact model alias noted by the customer and with identical generation settings (temperature, max_tokens, stop sequences).
> Result: I did not observe '###' tokens in 200 replayed calls. Outputs look structurally fine.

Observations and hypothesis:
- The pattern '###' suggests either an escaped token sequence from a client-side concatenation, or a partial chunk boundary in streaming mode that got re-joined incorrectly by the client.
- I checked our streaming buffer metrics around the customer's reported timestamp (2027-04-29T15:42:xxZ) and saw no dropped frames or retry bursts.
- No platform-level tokenizer errors or model crashes in the relevant time window.

Attachments: rishi_local-repro-logs.txt (contains request hashes and checksums for my replay runs).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Request a small set (5-10) of full raw request/response pairs from the customer including HTTP headers and whether they used chunked transfer / streaming.
2) If streaming was used, have the customer capture the raw TCP/HTTP stream for one failing example or switch to non-streaming for a short window for comparison.

I'll continue monitoring. If required we can enable enhanced per-request tracing for a limited window for Orion Health to capture additional diagnostics.

—Rishi
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Campos <nadia@orionhealth.io>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-30T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Strange '###' tokens appearing in generated notes

Hi Nadia — thanks for staying on this. I completed a platform-side scan across the customer's tenancy and recent request ids. Summary:

- We found three requests in the one-week window with anomalous response length (short truncated responses) but none containing '###'. Truncations correlated with client-initiated connection resets (TCP RST) from a single IP at the customer's side.
- No tokenizer or model-level anomalies in our logs.

Temporary mitigation steps for Orion Health to try:
- If possible, toggle to non-streaming responses for 24 hours to see if the artifact disappears.
- Add a simple post-processing filter: replace repeated sequences of non-alphanumeric characters longer than 3 with a single dash (this is a short-term workaround, not ideal).

If you can share one raw failing HTTP stream (headers + body) we'll ingest it into our tracing flow and run a byte-for-byte diff against our emitted stream. If we still can't reproduce after that, we can schedule a joint debugging session with a packet capture.

Attachment: platform_trace_excerpt.log

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Campos <nadia@orionhealth.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-30T16:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Strange '###' tokens appearing in generated notes — summary & next steps

Nadia — following up with a short summary and proposed closure path.

What we did:
- Replayed the customer's prompt 200x against the same model alias and generation settings (no reproduction).
- Scanned platform logs for tokenizer errors and streaming buffer issues in the reported windows (no evidence).
- Found signs of client-side connection resets correlated with a subset of short/truncated responses.

What we believe:
- Most likely the artifact is introduced after Redwood has produced the token stream — either in the customer's streaming client reassembly logic or a proxy between Orion Health and our endpoints.

Action items for Orion Health (recommended):
1) Capture one full raw failing HTTP stream (headers + body) and send to support (we'll ingest and compare bytes).
2) Temporarily switch to non-streaming responses for a 24-hour test window.
3) If you want, we can enable enhanced tracing on your tenancy for a 2-hour window while you exercise reproducing requests (requires authorization).

If we don't receive the raw stream within 7 days, we'll close this ticket as 'could not reproduce' but remain available to reopen if new evidence arrives. We want to avoid leaving unbounded tracing enabled.

Please let me know which option you prefer — quick debug session or the 24-hour non-streaming test. Happy to set up time this week.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
